summary: One row for every thing a person can see, set or press in today's app, and for every key it saves. The rows started from section 4 of the square-one audit (research/v7/square-one-audit.md) and were completed from the code: the test reads every key today's app saves straight from the code and the twelve test plans, so a new key fails the test until it has a row here.

**Built** means the /v7/ preview offers it, named by file. **Building now** marks work under way (none at present: the spending shape's steps and tapers are built, and its other parts are designed). **Designed** names the V7 document and section. **Planned** names the step that delivers it; "no V7 design yet" marks the ones no V7 document gives a place, which by the owner's rule stay unless the owner retires them. **Retired** gives the release-note reason; a retired option waits for the owner.

Where only part of a thing is in V7, the row is split (the part V7 has is built, the rest planned) or its note says what is missing. Line numbers are today's working copy (6.20.2) and will drift; the names beside them are the lasting reference. The spending shape's rows were checked in a browser on 2 Oct 2026, at 390 and 1280 px, beside today's planner's editor (guest only); the other rows' V7 files were read, not exercised.

rows.reason: Screen state saved with the line by accident, not a setting: V7 keeps open panels in the screen itself. Nothing a person set is lost.

rows.name: Steps by age: "from age X take £Y a year"
rows.what: The spending shape: each step is the total income wanted from an age on (State Pension, other pensions and the pot together), as many steps as wanted. One step is level for life.
rows.whereV6: Stress tester → Settings → Your income shape (index.html:3198-3215, 9118-9162; IncomeSchedule.js)
rows.note: A and B: on the spend step, under the figure, "Does what you spend change as you get older?" → "Change it with age": any number of steps by age (up to one a year of the plan), each a month after tax. C: the same block under "Add more detail", each step a share of what you start on. Each year's figure is today's own IncomeSchedule.amountAtAge (imported). A couple's ages are yours, with your partner's beside each step. Edited on a saved plan in V7 (editing-in-v7.md 8): the plan's own steps read a month after tax through the planner's tax sum and written back as the planner's rows.

rows.name: Add a step, remove a step
rows.what: "+ Add a step" adds one ten years after the last and £10,000 lower; any step but the first can be removed. No limit on how many.
rows.note: "+ Add a step" adds one 10 years after the last and 10% lower (today: £10,000 a year lower), and puts the keyboard in its age box; "Remove the step from 75" on every step after the first. No limit but one a year of the plan. Edited on a saved plan in V7 (editing-in-v7.md 8): the plan's own steps read a month after tax through the planner's tax sum and written back as the planner's rows.

rows.name: A taper within a step: falling by a real % a year
rows.what: Each step can fall each year by 0% to 5% in today's money, in quarter-point steps, compounding (£60,000 at 1% pays £59,400 the next year).
rows.whereV6: The slider on each step (index.html:9133-9136; IncomeSchedule.amountAtAge)
rows.note: Every step, the first included, "falls by …% a year": 0.25% to 10% in quarter points (today's slider stops at 5%), compounding at today's prices, by today's own amountAtAge. Edited on a saved plan in V7 (editing-in-v7.md 8): the plan's own steps read a month after tax through the planner's tax sum and written back as the planner's rows.

rows.name: A taper to the next step: glide evenly
rows.what: Instead of a cliff, a step can walk down in a straight line to the next step's amount, arriving as that step starts.
rows.whereV6: "glide evenly to the next step" on each step (index.html:9137; IncomeSchedule.amountAtAge)
rows.note: "moves evenly to the next step" on every step but the last: a straight line in pounds arriving as the next step starts, by today's own amountAtAge. Edited on a saved plan in V7 (editing-in-v7.md 8): the plan's own steps read a month after tax through the planner's tax sum and written back as the planner's rows.

rows.name: Go-go, go-slow and no-go years
rows.what: Explains the three phases of retirement spending, go-go (travel, projects, while fit), go-slow (from the mid-70s, typically drifting down 1-2% a year) and no-go (the basics, and care if it comes), and colours the years of the picture by phase (to 75, 75 to 85, 85 on).
rows.whereV6: Your income shape: the words above the steps and the bar colours (index.html:3199-3200; incomeShapeGraphic.js)
rows.note: The words above the steps name go-go (travel, projects), go-slow (from the mid-70s) and no-go (less again, though care can cost more); the picture draws the three bands at 75 and 85 (a couple: of the younger of you). The plan's "What you spend" step draws the same bands on its picture.

rows.name: Suggest go-slow and no-go steps
rows.what: One press adds suggested later steps from the first: 15% lower from 75 and 30% lower from 85, never below the budget's essentials, rounded to £500. Typical, not yours: edit freely.
rows.note: "Suggest go-go, go-slow and no-go years": today's suggestSteps in V7's units: 15% less from 75 and 30% less from 85, never below the budget's essentials, to the nearest £10 a month (today: £500 a year); for a couple, from when the younger of you is 75 and 85. Says what it filled in, and has Undo (today's has none). The preset "Slowly less" is today's old "declining with age" (smileToSteps). On a saved plan: the planner's own suggestSteps rule, function for function (tested against it), on the before-tax figures, said a month after tax; Cancel is the undo there.

rows.name: Start from my budget
rows.what: Sets the first step from the budget's total with tax added on.
rows.note: "Use £X a month" copies the budget's total into the figure (the budget stays a guide: owner, 1 Oct 2026); later steps are kept, as today, and "Move the later steps in proportion" is offered. On a saved plan: "Use £X a month at the start" fills the first row from the budget's cached total; a guide, never written.

rows.name: Start from a number
rows.what: Sets the first step from a figure typed in.
rows.note: The figure box on the spend step is the first amount; "The same every year" clears the steps (today's "or a number" replaces them all).

rows.name: The staircase picture
rows.what: Draws the shape as a bar for each year of age, coloured by go-go, go-slow and no-go, with a line along the tops.
rows.note: A bar a year from the start to the end of the plan, at 390 px with no sideways scroll; tap or point at a bar to read that year; "Show each year" opens a table. The motion as the steps change is its own row (income.staircase-motion), not built.

rows.name: The picture moves from the old shape to the new one
rows.what: When a step changes, the bars ease from their old heights to the new ones (about half a second) instead of jumping.
rows.note: Built (6.45.0): each bar of the picture eases from its old height to its new one over about half a second (a transition on the bars in the stylesheet; the bars keep their place by age across a redraw), and not at all for anyone who has asked their device for less motion (base.css). Built rather than retired: the owner's rule says no income-shape option may be retired.

rows.name: State Pension and other income as layers
rows.what: Inside each year's bar: the State Pension from its date, other income and a final-salary pension, income streams for their years, and on top what the pot must supply.
rows.note: On the answer's picture (A, B and C): each year's bar has the State Pension and other pensions (and pay or part-time work) after tax drawn lighter, and what the pension and savings pay darker, from the answer's own year-by-year rows. The same layers while the steps are set (income.layers-editing), the budget's total (income.budget-mark) and the markers for lump sums and one-off spends (income.markers) are rows of their own, not built.

rows.name: The layers while you set the steps
rows.what: As the steps are set, before any test is run, the picture already shows the State Pension and other income inside each bar, and what the pot must supply on top.
rows.note: Built on a saved plan's "What you spend": the rows of money that comes in anyway drawn under the steps while they are set (the plan's own year-by-year reading, no engine run).

rows.name: The budget's total marked on the picture
rows.what: A short line at the left of the picture marks the budget's total (with tax added), so the first step can be read against it.
rows.note: Built on a saved plan's "What you spend": a short dashed mark at the budget's total a month, named in the key, a guide only.

rows.name: Lump sums and one-off spends marked at their ages
rows.what: A lump sum arriving (▲) and a one-off spend (▼, with its years) are drawn on the picture at their ages, with their amounts.
rows.note: Built on a saved plan's "What you spend": a mark under the year of each lump sum coming in and each one-off spend going out, named in the key with its amount.

rows.name: Below the essentials turns orange
rows.what: The budget's essentials are a line on the picture; a step below them turns orange and a note says the floor strategies will not buy less than the bills.
rows.note: With a budget: the essentials are a dashed line, a year below them is marked in the warning colour, and a note says so in words ("That is allowed: it is your figure"). A guide only: never a floor (owner, 1 Oct 2026). The plan's "What you spend" step draws the budget's essentials dashed and says the first year below them.

rows.name: Never below guaranteed income
rows.what: A year whose step would fall below the income that arrives anyway (State Pension, other pensions) is held there, with a note from which age.
rows.note: The engine takes nothing from the pots in a year whose State Pension and other pensions (after tax) pay more than the step; the answer's note "shape-below-income" says from which age, and the picture shows that year's bar as the income itself. Today's editor also says it while the steps are set: that is its own row (income.below-income-live), not built.

rows.name: "Below the income you get anyway", said while setting the steps
rows.what: While the steps are set, an orange note says from which age a step is below the income that arrives anyway (State Pension, other pensions), which then pays instead.
rows.note: Built on a saved plan's "What you spend": "Below the income you get anyway from age N" said while the steps are set, from the same rows as the layers.

rows.name: Each later step as a share of the budget
rows.what: Beside each later step: its amount as a % of the budget (or of "your budget (a guide)" on a plan made from a V7 answer).
rows.note: Beside each later step: "85% of the start", and with a budget "85% of the start, 71% of your budget (a guide)", as today's "— 85% of today's budget".

rows.name: The first step's take-home a month
rows.what: Says what the first step leaves a month after tax at today's bands.
rows.note: Not needed as a separate line: every V7 figure is typed and shown after tax, a month (today's line turns its before-tax step into take-home). The answer's "what it is made of" shows the tax.

rows.name: Turn a lump sum into income
rows.what: For each lump sum: what it could add a year if spread over the years left, and one press to add that to the steps from its age (the lump stays as the money that pays for it).
rows.note: Built on "What you spend" (6.45.0): each lump sum inside the plan's years with what it could support a year over the years left (the planner's spendLumpSum lifted pure as IncomeSchedule.lumpIntoSteps; index.html calls it), and "Add £X a year from age N" — the step in force at that age raised and every later one too, a new step where none starts there — as the cards' edits (the draft, nothing written: each amount box the month after tax, the planner's before-tax figure riding beside it) so Save writes the steps the planner makes to the pound; the lump sum stays as the money that pays for it. Test T16 of tests/v7/screens/shapeParity.test.js is the identity in tests/v7/plan/rows11bSteps.test.js.

rows.name: Extra spends in a given year
rows.what: A car, a roof, a wedding: an amount drawn on top of the income shape in a plan year (or several), taxed like income, which every strategy must fund.
rows.whereV6: Income streams & lump sums: + Extra spend (index.html:10636-10637)
rows.note: Built on a saved plan's "What you spend" step (editing-in-v7.md 8): one-off costs as cards — what it is, the amount a year after tax at today's prices, at an age, for how many years, going up with prices or a fixed sum — written as the planner's extraWithdrawals rows (the before-tax amount the planner's marginal sum on top of that year's figure, the plan year from the age). Not yet on the questions' spend step (spending-shape.md §16 still stands for that).

rows.name: The year-by-year figure every tool reads
rows.what: The shape compiled to one figure a year from the plan's start age, read by every strategy, the stress tests and the Decision tool; the first step is the Decision tool's target.
rows.note: Every V7 answer (C, A, B) works out each year's figure from the shape and tests it year by year. "Save this as a plan" writes seed version 3 for a shaped answer, and today's planner turns it into its own income steps (compressSteps) that give the answer's after-tax figure in every year, to the pound. Written with the steps by the plan's "What you spend" step: the planner's compiledTargetSchedule rule (floored by the income you get anyway, rounded), and the Decision copies, as the planner's Save does.

rows.name: Amounts before tax, in today's money
rows.what: Every step is £ a year before tax at today's prices; tax comes out of it.
rows.note: V7 asks after tax, a month (square-one-audit.md §5); the kept plan carries today's before-tax, a-year steps, each year grossed up by today's own grossUpAnnual, so both readings hold.

rows.name: What you want to spend, take-home, a month or a year
rows.what: The spending need typed as take-home, a month or a year, with the gross worked out and a chip to use the budget's figure.
rows.whereV6: Decision tool → Settings → Spending need (index.html:2553-2575); the hidden Stress box
rows.note: One figure a month after tax, or a national level. Today's box also takes the figure a year; V7 asks a month only.

rows.name: Age today
rows.what: Your age now, dated, which with the State Pension date pins every plan year to a tax year and an age.
rows.whereV6: Stress → Settings → When your plan starts (index.html:3150-3166)
rows.note: Asked in every question; edited on a saved plan in V7 ("About you and when", editing-in-v7.md).

rows.name: Retired already, or retiring at an age
rows.what: "I have already retired" or "I will retire at age X".
rows.whereV6: Stress → Settings → When your plan starts (index.html:3153-3154)
rows.note: A and B ask the stop age (or "I've already stopped"); C asks when the money starts. Edited on a saved plan in V7: stopped, or stopping at an age or a month ("About you and when").

rows.name: Plan starts this tax year or next April
rows.what: Which tax year is the plan's year 0; months before it are bridge months, lived on cash.
rows.note: In V7, on a saved plan ("About you and when", editing-in-v7.md): "When the plan's income starts: this tax year / next April" for someone who has stopped; derived from the stop age otherwise, and said so. The Decision copy (decision.firstTaxYear) is kept in step as the planner's Save keeps it.

rows.name: Pots at retirement, projected
rows.what: For someone still working, projects the pots to the retirement age from today's pots and payments.
rows.whereV6: When your plan starts: the projection line (index.html:8953-8957)
rows.note: Better: the saving-years engine gives a middling and a bad case.

rows.name: Pots at retirement, typed in
rows.what: Overrides the projection with the pension and ISA you expect to have on the day, in today's money.
rows.whereV6: When your plan starts: "Or SIPP at retirement", "ISA at retirement" (index.html:3160-3161)
rows.note: A plan made from a V7 answer writes the middling pot here (PlanSeed.js); the plan step lets the person type it. Edited on a saved plan in V7 ("Your pots and tax", editing-in-v7.md 9): each fact once, the saved value and source beside it, written as the planner's own key. No V7 question asks for it yet.

rows.name: How long the plan runs
rows.what: The plan's length in years (the age it runs to).
rows.whereV6: Stress → Settings → Duration; Decision → Depletion Duration
rows.note: Asked as the age to plan to (endAge, 75 to 105, 95 by default); edited on a saved plan in V7 as "Plan to age" ("About you and when").

rows.name: Suggest a plan length from longevity
rows.what: Suggests the length from age and sex: a 1-in-10 chance of living beyond (cautious), 1 in 4, or average.
rows.note: In V7 as "Suggest from how long people live" on "About you and when": a man or a woman, 1 in 10 / 1 in 4 / half live beyond it; the planner's own helper (LongevityModel.longevityAge) fills "Plan to age".

rows.name: "Update this draft to today"
rows.what: A draft whose start year has passed is offered an update to today; "Leave it" is remembered.
rows.note: Built on "About you and when" (6.45.0): a draft whose start year has passed (PlanTiming.staleDraft, the planner's own rule on the plan as read — never locked, never with a month recorded) is offered "Update it to start in <this tax year>" (the boxes the planner's update sets — stopped, this tax year — then the ordinary save, so the steps, the figures by year and the Decision tool's first year move with it) and "Leave it" (one write of stress.staleDraftDismissedFor, remembered for that year; op 'stale', with Undo). The plan page's next sentence (P.stale) links to the step.

rows.name: Pension pot, split into shares, bonds and cash
rows.what: The pension total and how it splits into the three pots the plan draws from; their floors run down over the plan (the glidepath).
rows.whereV6: Stress and Decision → Settings → Your allocation (index.html:3329-3333)
rows.note: V7 asks the pension total; the split follows the risk level. Edited on a saved plan in V7 ("Your pots and tax", editing-in-v7.md 9): each fact once, the saved value and source beside it, written as the planner's own key.

rows.name: Risk level: cautious, balanced, adventurous
rows.what: Sets the mix of shares, bonds and cash, or switches to testing a list of funds.
rows.whereV6: Your allocation: Pick a risk level / Test on a list of funds (index.html:3303-3306, 3379-3393)
rows.note: V7 has a risk level while drawing and another while saving.

rows.name: Test on a list of funds
rows.what: A list of funds, each tagged to a bucket and a sub-class (searched, typed or pasted from a platform), becomes the allocation the plan is tested on. Each strategy keeps its own list.
rows.whereV6: Your allocation → Test on a list of funds (index.html:3407-3430; PortfolioTagger.js, FundCatalogue.js)
rows.note: Built on "The mix" (#/plan/<id>/mix): "As the funds to test" — typed with the bundled search, or pasted from a platform with "What is this?" for each line not recognised and "Left out, and why"; each line counted as shares, bonds, gold and trend, or cash; the list becomes the split the plan is tested on (PortfolioTagger.mixFromFunds, the planner's own); one list per way of drawing (the stash). Not a record of what is held.

rows.name: An example ETF portfolio for the risk level
rows.what: Shows an illustrative fund portfolio for the chosen level (not advice).
rows.whereV6: "See an example ETF portfolio for this level" (index.html:3398-3401; ModelPortfolios.js)
rows.note: Built: "Show an example list for this level (not advice)" on "The mix" — the planner's model list for the level, filling nothing in.

rows.name: Diversifiers sleeve: gold and trend/macro
rows.what: Carves a slice into assets that tend to hold up when shares fall, held flat and sold first in a downturn; the target rises with prices and runs down like the others.
rows.note: Built: "Keep a slice in gold and trend funds" (yes/no) on "The mix", with "What it does in a bad case" — one run of the one test with the slice the other way, the bad-case figure beside the plan's own.

rows.name: Bond tent
rows.what: Shares rise over time: bond-heavy early, when the pot is largest and most exposed to an early crash, share-heavy later, centred on the risk level; a tagged plan sets its end mix.
rows.note: Built: "Use the bond tent" (yes/no) on "The mix", the sentence with the plan's own years, "What it does in a bad case" (one run), the level the tent rises to for a funds list; "Buckets in order ignores the tent" said.

rows.name: ISA (and savings) total
rows.what: The ISA held beside the pension, drawn as its own pot.
rows.whereV6: Your allocation: Total in your ISA (index.html:3335)
rows.note: Asked as savings (ISAs and other savings). Edited on a saved plan in V7 ("Your pots and tax", editing-in-v7.md 9): each fact once, the saved value and source beside it, written as the planner's own key.

rows.name: How the ISA is used
rows.what: Tax-efficient (tops up income before higher-rate tax), make it last to the State Pension, or hold it (never drawn for income; it still rescues a plan whose pension runs out).
rows.whereV6: Your allocation: How the ISA is used (index.html:3337-3343)
rows.note: Edited on a saved plan in V7 ("Your pots and tax", editing-in-v7.md 9): each fact once, the saved value and source beside it, written as the planner's own key. No V7 question asks for it yet.

rows.name: How the ISA and savings grow, and the ISA's floor
rows.what: One choice per plan: "Mostly cash" (the default; like the pension's cash, last year's rise in prices less 1%, never below nothing) or "Invested like my pension" (the pension's mix of shares, bonds and cash, in the same futures). A plan locked before the choice keeps a fixed 3% a year (isaReturn) until it is unlocked. Also the floor the ISA is drawn down towards (isaMin).
rows.whereV6: Stress tester → Settings → How your ISA and savings grow (index.html #ssIsaGrowthGroup; src/ui/isaGrowthSetting.js, src/services/IsaGrowth.js); the floor in the settings defaults (constants.js ISA_DEFAULTS)
rows.note: One choice under the savings box in C, A and B ("Mostly cash" or "Invested like my pension"), carried between them and into a plan made from the answer; today's planner has the same choice in Stress tester → Settings from 6.22.0 (schema version 3 writes "Mostly cash" into every unlocked plan). The floor (isaMin) is saved but read by no engine in either app: both draw the ISA down to nothing. Edited on a saved plan in V7 ("Your pots and tax", editing-in-v7.md 9): each fact once, the saved value and source beside it, written as the planner's own key.

rows.name: A taxable account (GIA)
rows.what: Money held outside a pension or ISA: how much, what it holds (shares, gilts, bond funds, a mix, cash) and the tax band it is taxed at; it is drawn first and taxed each year.
rows.whereV6: Your allocation: Taxable investments today (index.html:3347-3376; TaxableSleeve.js)
rows.note: answer-D.md §9.2 reads the ordinary account from a locked plan's holdings; the plan step asks for it. Edited on a saved plan in V7 ("Your pots and tax", editing-in-v7.md 9): each fact once, the saved value and source beside it, written as the planner's own key. No V7 question asks for it yet.

rows.name: Charges (funds and platform), % a year
rows.what: One charge a year taken off monthly from funds and cash, while saving and while drawing.
rows.note: Edited on a saved plan in V7 ("Your pots and tax", editing-in-v7.md 9): each fact once, the saved value and source beside it, written as the planner's own key.

rows.name: State Pension amount
rows.what: The State Pension from the forecast: full, a forecast amount, or none.
rows.whereV6: Stress and Decision → Settings → State Pension (index.html:3546-3561)
rows.note: Asked in every question; edited on a saved plan in V7 ("Money that comes in anyway", editing-in-v7.md 7): the full amount, the forecast's weekly amount, or none — and, while a plan has no figure, "as the planner assumes" (its old yearly figure from age 67), said in the planner's own words.

rows.name: State Pension start date, typed from the forecast
rows.what: The exact date it starts, as on the forecast (also the birthday the plan reckons ages from).
rows.note: Built on "Money that comes in anyway" (6.45.0): the date box under the State Pension choice, shown while a State Pension is chosen, holding the saved text; read by the planner's own parser (StatePensionUtils.validateStatePensionDate, a date of birth refused in its own words) and written as the day to stress.spStartDate, and to decision.spStartDate only where the Decision settings already carry it (an absent setting means the old behaviour); the saved text typed back writes nothing; a plan with no date that gains a State Pension still gets the day its State Pension age is reached unless a date is typed.

rows.name: The old State Pension fields
rows.what: The State Pension as an annual figure from a plan year, from before the start date was asked; read only when a plan has no date.
rows.note: Built, reading (6.26): a plan with no State Pension date shows its yearly figure and the tax year it starts (firstTaxYear + statePensionYear), as the planner reads it; never asked. Written by "Money that comes in anyway" as PlanSeed writes it: 0 for none (else every run assumes £12,000), the yearly figure beside a weekly amount.

rows.name: Final-salary pension: amount and start
rows.what: A defined-benefit pension: how much a year, in today's money, and when it starts.
rows.whereV6: Other income: Defined-Benefit Pension, starts at an age (the plan year is derived and saved beside it; src/ui/dbStartSetting.js)
rows.note: Better: V7 asks the start by age, not plan year, for each person. Edited on a saved plan in V7 as cards by start age (editing-in-v7.md 7): the first is the planner's own keys (the year from the age, the age beside it); a second or third goes into the planner's "income for some years" list as income for the rest of the plan, labelled "Final-salary pension".

rows.name: How a final-salary pension rises
rows.what: Rises with prices capped at 5%, with full prices, or not at all.
rows.note: V7's household takes all three (household.js) but the question forms always say prices capped at 5%. Edited on a saved plan in V7 with all three ("Money that comes in anyway", editing-in-v7.md 7).

rows.name: Other income or pension
rows.what: Another taxable income a year from now, rising with prices capped at 4%.
rows.note: D designs income you have bought (answer-D.md §5.2); no question form asks a general other income. Edited on a saved plan in V7 ("Money that comes in anyway", editing-in-v7.md 7): other income for the whole plan, a year before tax, rising with prices capped at 4%.

rows.name: Part-time work for some years
rows.what: Earnings for a number of years after stopping.
rows.note: A's "Would some part-time work help?"; D designs the same for the retired (answer-D.md §3.6).

rows.name: Income for some years
rows.what: Any taxable income between two plan years (rent that ends, part-time work, a small pension), with how it rises.
rows.whereV6: Stress → Settings → Income streams & lump sums (index.html:3535-3545, 10635-10641)
rows.note: Only part-time work from the stop is asked in the questions (row above). Edited on a saved plan in V7 as cards ("Money that comes in anyway", editing-in-v7.md 7): what it is, the amount a year before tax, from age, to age or for the rest of the plan, how it rises — by age, stored as the planner's plan years.

rows.name: One-off lump sums
rows.what: Money arriving in a plan year (an inheritance, downsizing): where it can legally go (ISA allowance, pension up to earnings or the £10,000 limit, the rest taxable), what it is held in, and the Decision tool's advice in its year.
rows.whereV6: Income streams & lump sums: + One-off lump sum (index.html:10639-10660; TaxableSleeve.routeWindfall)
rows.note: Built on "Money that comes in anyway" (6.41.0 the cards, 6.45.0 where each lands): what it is, the amount, at age, what kind — the saved plan's windfalls rows kept byte for byte where unchanged — and under each card where it lands in its year, the planner's own note (TaxableSleeve.routeWindfall: an inherited pension to the pension, an inherited ISA to the ISA, a cash lump sum to the ISA allowance unless the ISA is on hold, the pension within its room, the rest a taxable account held as the plan's mix or the row's own). The Decision tool's advice in its year stays on the classic page (month.advice). The question forms' "Money you expect to come in" (spending-shape.md §17) is a design for the questions, not a planner option.

rows.name: Tax thresholds
rows.what: Personal allowance, basic-rate limit and higher-rate limit for year 0, which can be changed.
rows.note: V7's questions use today's bands (toEngine.js BANDS); a saved plan's bands are changed on the plan step. Edited on a saved plan in V7 ("Your pots and tax", editing-in-v7.md 9): each fact once, the saved value and source beside it, written as the planner's own key. No V7 question asks for it yet.

rows.name: Thresholds rise with prices, or stay frozen
rows.what: Whether the tax bands rise with inflation or stay where they are.
rows.note: Edited on a saved plan in V7 ("Your pots and tax", editing-in-v7.md 9): each fact once, the saved value and source beside it, written as the planner's own key. No V7 question asks for it yet.

rows.name: The 25% tax-free part: in each withdrawal, or kept separate

rows.name: Buckets in order
rows.what: Cash pays first, then bonds, then shares; surplus refills from above when it is more than a set band over its path. Dials: the band, and the pension and ISA totals.

rows.what: Buys index-linked gilts for the first years of income and rides the rest in shares, selling only when shares are well above their path or on a calendar. Dials: years bought, the income bolted on, the trigger, the band, the pension and ISA totals.
rows.note: Built (6.40.0): the card with the years bought up front, the income bolted on, when it buys more years (the band or every five years), the band — every dial the planner shows; the pots are the plan's.

rows.name: Bridge & engine
rows.what: Every year to the bridge age (usually the State Pension) bought now, cash first then one gilt a year; the rest rides in shares untouched, then pays by withdrawals. Dials: the bridge age, years in cash, the pension and ISA totals.

rows.note: Built (6.40.0): the card with the age the years are bought to and the years paid from cash first; the pots are the plan's.

rows.name: Floor & Flex
rows.what: Buys the essentials as a floor to an age with gilts; the rest is a flex sleeve paying a set share each year; booms can extend or raise the floor. Dials: essentials, the floor's end age, the sleeve rate, the treats rule, the ratchet, the pension and ISA totals.
rows.note: Built (6.40.0): the card with the bills a year, the age they are paid to, what the rest pays out (1–10% in quarter steps — the engine's range, wider than the Settings box), the treats rule and the ratchet (kept with the plan; the one test runs the floor without it, said on the card). The bills are never filled from the budget.

Dials: the age, the borrowed floor, the pension and ISA totals.

rows.note: Built (6.40.0): the card with the age the income is bought to; the borrowed floor is the rotation's record, written by its switch on the classic page, never a dial.
